subject: HIPAA/BAA eligibility and deployment options - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@medwisehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility and deployment options - next steps

Hi Alyssa -

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

TL;DR: Redwood can support HIPAA-covered workloads if a BAA is in place and the customer chooses an eligible deployment mode (Dedicated or Private). Hosted (public) API is not eligible for PHI.

Recap: 
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (in progress to next annual cycle); security evidence can be shared via our secure drive.
- BAA: Redwood offers a standard BAA for customers handling PHI. Legal typically has a 3-4 business day review for the standard agreement; we can fast-track if needed.
- PHI handling boundaries: Redwood's hosted public endpoints do not accept PHI. PHI-in-scope options are: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with isolated tenancy) or Private (VPC/on-prem). Both support customer KMS and audit logging.
- Questionnaire: You mentioned a 3rd-party vendor security questionnaire - happy to start that. I've attached a short HIPAA/BAA summary and an initial vendor security questionnaire stub for your team to fill.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You: confirm whether MedWise will handle PHI in the initial integration and share the questionnaire (or we can send one).
2) Redwood: share SOC 2 evidence and standard BAA draft (attached).
3) Tech sync: schedule a 30-min call with your infra/security to review deployment modes and KMS/audit expectations. Neha and Dev will join.

Open items / questions for you: 
- Do you expect any PHI fields to be sent to Redwood at launch, or will you be passing only de-identified data?
- Preferred timeline for legal review (we can include a redline turnaround SLA in the SOW if helpful).

Attachments: hipaa_baa_summary.pdf (short summary of eligible deployment modes + BAA process), vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf (fillable stub).

Thanks - I'll follow up with SOC 2 evidence links once I get signoff from security.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap - very helpful. A few answers and requests from our side: 

1) PHI scope: For MVP we expect to transmit patient identifiers and limited clinical notes (so yes, PHI in-scope).
2) Questionnaire: attaching the vendor security questionnaire you requested - it's slightly longer than your stub. Could your security team fill the technical sections (architecture, encryption, logging) and legal review the BAA?
3) Timeline: We'd like to aim for a mid-April go/no-go on the integration; legal review ideally completed within 2 weeks of receiving the BAA draft.

A couple of clarifying questions: 
- For Dedicated: can you confirm whether we get tenant-level network isolation and a customer-managed KMS?
- For Private (VPC): do you support deployment into our AWS account or only into a Redwood-managed VPC? Any differences in audit log access?

Attaching: MedWise_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Fillable.pdf

Thanks - Jordan (our Head of Security) will be the day-to-day on this and may follow up with more detailed items.

Best,
Alyssa
Director, Product Partnerships | MedWise Health
alyssa@medwisehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility and deployment options - next steps

Hi Alyssa -

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the completed questionnaire - we started a row-by-row response. High-level answers to your technical questions below; Dev/Neha will follow up with architecture notes and logging/KMS specifics.

- Dedicated: Yes - Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and tenant-level network controls. Customers can opt for customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. Audit logs (access + request traces) are available and can be streamed to your SIEM.
- Private (VPC): We support both Redwood-managed VPCs and deployments into customer-owned AWS accounts (VPC peering / dedicated subnets). Deploying into your AWS account gives you direct VPC control and access to CloudTrail/CloudWatch logs; Redwood-managed VPC still provides full audit log exports but requires cross-account roles for access.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll send the standard BAA draft to your legal as an initial cadence today (expect a DocuSign link) and copy Jordan.
- Neha will share SOC 2 evidence and the completed security questionnaire answers by EOD tomorrow.
- Dev will propose a short technical rundown (30 min) for next week to confirm network/KMS setup.

Let us know preferred times for the tech sync.

Best,
Marissa

Following up with the items Marissa promised. I've uploaded the SOC 2 evidence bundle and our BAA draft to a secure link (Doc link below). See answers to a few common flags below - we'll include more detailed notes in the questionnaire responses.

Quick answers: 
- SOC 2: We are SOC 2 Type II certified (most recent report: 2027-11); I'll share the attestation and our SOC 2 bridge letter.
- BAA turnaround: Standard review is 3-4 business days; if redlines are needed we'll route to legal and typically complete within 7-10 business days depending on complexity.
- Logging/KMS: For Dedicated the customer-managed KMS option supports BYOK; audit logs include token-level traces, request metadata, and operator actions. For Private deployments into customer accounts you will retain full CloudTrail/CloudWatch access.
